name: People forget abstract information
description: Important ideas are not remembered because they are too vague, complex, or disconnected from experience.

name: Plans fail in unpredictable environments
description: Detailed instructions become ineffective when circumstances change and unexpected events occur.

name: Too many competing priorities
description: Organizations struggle to align decisions when multiple goals compete for attention.

name: Teams struggle to make consistent decisions
description: Large groups of people make inconsistent choices when they lack a clear guiding principle for evaluating decisions.

name: Burying the lead
description: Communicators obscure the most important idea by placing it too late or allowing details to overshadow the central message.

name: Loss of message focus
description: Communicators become absorbed in details and lose sight of the central idea that matters most to the audience.

name: Decision paralysis under uncertainty
description: People struggle to make decisions when faced with uncertainty, complexity, or multiple competing possibilities.

name: Message dilution
description: A communication loses impact because too many important messages compete for attention at the same time.

name: Strategic priorities fail to influence behavior
description: Organizations know what matters but fail to communicate priorities in a way that consistently guides day-to-day decisions.

name: Experts resist simplification
description: People with deep expertise often avoid simplifying ideas because they fear losing nuance or appearing superficial.

name: Compact messages without substance
description: Messages become memorable but unhelpful when they are concise without reflecting an important core truth.

name: Feature overload
description: Products become difficult to use because additional features accumulate and dilute the original purpose.

name: Information exceeds memory capacity
description: People struggle to remember information when it is presented as disconnected data rather than meaningful concepts.

name: Difficulty understanding unfamiliar concepts
description: People struggle to learn new ideas when they cannot connect them to existing knowledge.

name: Complex information overwhelms learners
description: Large amounts of information become difficult to understand or remember when presented without structure.

name: Accurate but unusable communication
description: Information is technically correct but too abstract, complex, or detailed to help people make decisions.

name: New ideas are difficult to communicate
description: People struggle to understand unfamiliar concepts because they lack existing mental models for interpreting them.

name: Organizational values fail to guide behavior
description: Companies create slogans or labels that do not provide actionable guidance for employee decisions and behavior.

name: People ignore familiar messages
description: Audiences tune out communications that follow predictable patterns they have encountered repeatedly.

name: Failure to sustain attention
description: Messages briefly capture attention but fail to keep audiences engaged long enough to communicate their ideas.
